To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the DGLAP evolution of the structure functions is not sufficient for the description of the HERA and RHIC data, and that the inclusion of the first nonlinear terms in the DGLAV evolution equations is necessary.

the DGLAP equation with the first nonlinear corrections, the DGLAP plus GLRMQ approach, describes well the HERA data in the region 1 < x < 100, 0.3 < Q2 < 10^4 GeV^2, and 10^-3 < z < 1, with the saturation limits determined for the proton and the lead.

(i) the first nonlinear corrections do not change the DGLAP predictions at HERA, (ii) the saturation limits are not reached in the DGLP+GLRMQ model at HERA, and (iii) the saturation limits in the DGLDP+GLRMQ are higher than those in the DGLD model.
